key_insight: In lead-halide perovskite nanocrystals, strong coupling to a developing lattice-polarization field does not just renormalize excitons—it creates new excitonic states and later coherent coupling between them.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar cells and optoelectronic devices, this means exciton dynamics, radiative strength, and coherence can depend on time-dependent polaron formation, so device models must include lattice back-action, not only static excitons.
method: Femtosecond coherent multidimensional spectroscopy on lead-halide perovskite nanocrystals
Compare perovskites against CdSe quantum dots as a weak-coupling control
Fit observations with a dynamical polaron-field model
evidence_signal: The abstract reports time-resolved diagonal and anti-diagonal spectral splittings that grow with nanocrystal size and track radiative oscillator strength, plus delayed appearance of X2 and X1–X2 coherence.
watch_item: The effect is demonstrated in nanocrystals under ultrafast spectroscopy, so translating it to full solar-cell operating conditions will require care about morphology, temperature, and timescale differences.
paper_title: Quantum Back-Action Expands the Excitonic Hilbert Space in a Soft Polar Semiconductor
